Residential HVAC system, trane 4tec3F60B. Initially stopped working due to a clogged drain in the pan, kept shutting the unit off. Alter getting it looked at, it's running a high head pressure (450 supposedly 80 psi out of spec). Low side PSI is fine. Run cap is running warm, and tests at 66 instead of 70. TD is 17* which should be fine.

What gives? Filter is clean, replaced it and it didn't make any difference.
HVAC residential, high head pressure, why?

High head pressure is the liquid line backing up. So from your condenser to evaporator. Dirty evaporator, condenser, or filter. Take a temp check at your filter dryer, before it and after it. If it has a big temp difference, it means that your dryer is clogged.
